=== 59475 Motion for Info Prehearing Conference, Bifurcation of Hearing, & Geographical Alignment.docx ===
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC Docket No. 59475 

COMMISSION STAFF’S MOTION FOR informational prehearing conference and for alignment of intervenors in Order of Presentation 
On March 26, 2026, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (collectively, Applicants) filed a joint application with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) to amend their respective certificates of convenience and necessity (CCNs) for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kilovolt (kV) transmission line project. 
On April 20, 2026, the administrative law judges (ALJs) from the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) filed SOAH Order No. 6, establishing a procedural schedule, including a deadline of June 3, 2026 for parties to make pre-hearing submissions of witness lists, exhibit lists, and exhibits, and for the Applicants to file a proposed order of presentation. On May 8, 2026, the SOAH ALJs filed SOAH Order No. 12, consolidating this docket with Docket No. 59182, regarding the issue of need for Import Path 2, which is a common issue to both proceedings. 
On May 18, 2026, the SOAH ALJs filed SOAH Order No. 15, rescheduling the prehearing conference from June 8, 2026, to June 5, 2026, to make best use of time for the hearing that is scheduled for June 8, 2026. Therefore, in line with the intent of SOAH Order No. 15, Commission Staff (Staff) respectfully files this motion for the further processing of this docket.
MOTION FOR INFORMATIONAL PREHEARING CONFERENCE
As an initial matter, Staff agrees with the rescheduling of the prehearing conference to be a full day in advance of the first day of the hearing. And while the prehearing conference has been scheduled to begin at 1:00 pm on June 5, 2026, Staff respectfully requests that there be consideration from the parties and the SOAH ALJs as to whether an earlier start time would be more useful. Notably, given the amount of parties and testimonies in this proceeding, the time for offering and admitting initial exhibits may take longer than allowed by a 1:00 pm start time. 
In the same regard, due to the large number of parties that are unrepresented in this docket, Staff notes that there has been a high volume of procedural inquiries directed to Staff throughout this proceeding. While Staff readily welcomes and answers such inquiries, except to the extent the Texas Rules of Professional Conduct prohibits Staff from offering legal advice, for the benefit of the further processing of this docket before the hearing, Staff respectfully requests that an informational prehearing conference be scheduled for June 3, 2026, or earlier, so that unrepresented parties can be wholly, effectively, and consistently informed about the pre-hearing submissions required in SOAH Order No. 6, as well as other procedural matters for participating in the hearing on the merits.
While Staff does not oppose the issuance of an order regarding same, Staff posits that such prehearing conference would serve not only as an informational presentation directed to unrepresented parties but also serve as an opportunity for such parties to ask technical questions and see demonstrations regarding administrative and procedural matters, such as the Applicants’ file-sharing site, if any, SOAH’s Kiteworks, and exhibit lists. Further, it would also help to provide any needed explanations regarding the pre-hearing submissions in advance of such deadline to make better use of the time for the prehearing conference. Moreover, an informational prehearing conference would make best use the time for the hearing by providing an overview of the hearing process that (1) gives unrepresented parties a better understanding of how to participate going into the hearing, (2) reduces time spent on live objections, and (3) addresses any concerns from the unrepresented parties regarding the overall process. 
MOTION for alignment of intervenors in Order of Presentation
Due to the large number of potential intervenors that will participate at the hearing on the merits, Staff respectfully requests that there be some form of alignment to better help the hearing process and record. Specifically, while alignment of parties has been required in prior transmission line cases of this magnitude, Staff does not suggest nor does it oppose that intervenors be required to align in this proceeding. Instead, Staff suggests that in developing the order of presentation, the Applicants be required to align the intervenors geographically, such as by route links. 
This would give such groups the option of either aligning and designating a representative for purposes of cross-examining witnesses or coordinating on an order of cross-examination. And if such alignment or coordination does not occur or is not feasible, the ordering of cross-examination could be determined at random through a random number generator or similar tool for fairness. Altogether, this would (1) importantly ensure that parties are given an equitable amount of time to participate, (2) allow for set hearing dates so that parties may better plan their schedules, and (3) support efficient division of time by allowing parties to discuss amongst their smaller geographical groups. 
In addition to the proposed alignment of geographical party groups, Staff further respectfully requests that the issue of need be bifurcated from the routing issues. More particularly, since need is an issue that is common to both this docket and Docket No. 59182, it would be appropriate to consider such issue as its own separate phase from the routing phase of the hearing. Furthermore, to the extent that parties contest the issue of need for these consolidated projects, Staff respectfully requests that such parties be required to identify whether they intend to participate on the need phase for purposes of developing the order of presentation.  
CONCLUSION
For the reasons detailed above, Staff respectfully requests the entry of an order (1) addressing  whether the prehearing conference on June 5, 2026, should start at an earlier time, (2) scheduling an informational prehearing conference for June 3, 2026, or earlier, to assist unrepresented parties in better understanding and navigating the process, (3) bifurcating the issue of need into its own phase for the hearing, and (4) requiring the Applicants to align the intervenors geographically for purposes of developing the order of presentation.

Dated: May 19, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
